query: Sodium-ion batteries United States customs classification duties

statements.text: In the United States, lithium-ion batteries face a combined import tariff exceeding 100%, factoring in base duties, anti-dumping measures, and Section 301 tariffs. In contrast, sodium-ion batteries are currently subject to a total import duty of just 38.4%
Sodium-ion batteries have no lithium, cobalt, or nickel – making them entirely insulated from the tariff pressures affecting lithium-based chemistries.
Yes. Sodium-ion cells and batteries covered by the applicable entries must satisfy the relevant UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, part III, subsection 38.3 requirements.
Sodium-ion batteries with aqueous alkaline electrolyte fall under a different entry entirely, UN2795 (Batteries, wet, filled with alkali), which is Class 8 corrosive, not Class 9.

For sodium-ion, the 67th edition of the IATA DGR introduced UN3551 (batteries shipped alone) and UN3552 (batteries packed with or contained in equipment) for cells and batteries with organic electrolyte.
